svg.title: test_random_seed_is_locked_at_692_across_all_notebooks
svg.desc: Two-section diagram showing first an anatomy of the regular expression pattern that matches RANDOM_SEED equals digit declarations with whitespace tolerance and a capture group around the digits, and then a loop visualization across all six notebooks NB01 through NB06 with each one passing the assertion that its captured value equals the string 692, followed by a counter-example showing what would happen if any notebook drifted to a different seed.
svg.text: Test 1 — every notebook must declare RANDOM_SEED = 692
For each of the 6 notebooks: read source → pattern.findall(source) → assert each captured value == "692"
The \s* in the pattern tolerates any spacing — RANDOM_SEED=692 and RANDOM_SEED = 692 both work.
The parentheses around \d+ make it a CAPTURE group — findall returns just the digits, not the whole match.
If a notebook contains the variable name in a docstring without an equals sign, the pattern simply does not match it.
All six notebooks now pass this check. CI run #191: 14 passed in 12.24s.
